```plato
    // V = 0 is the base rim, V = 1 the apex (where the U circle degenerates to a
    // point, so the last row of a UV quad grid is a fan of slivers).
    Eval(s: Cone, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var f = AxisFrame(s.Apex, s.Axis);
        var p = PointOnCircle(uv.U.Turns, s.Radius * (1.0 - uv.V));
        return f.PointInFrame(Point3D(p.X, p.Y, s.Height * (1.0 - uv.V)));
    }
    ClosedU(s: Cone): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Cone): Boolean => false;

    // The lateral wall, radius interpolating from BottomRadius at V = 0 to
    // TopRadius at V = 1.
    Eval(s: ConicalFrustum, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var f = AxisFrame(s.Center, s.Axis);
        var p = PointOnCircle(uv.U.Turns, s.BottomRadius.Lerp(s.TopRadius, uv.V));
        return f.PointInFrame(Point3D(p.X, p.Y, (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Height));
    }
    ClosedU(s: ConicalFrustum): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: ConicalFrustum): Boolean => false;

    // Cylindrical side plus two hemispherical caps: V crosses the A-end cap over
    // [0, 0.25], the side over [0.25, 0.75], and the B-end cap over [0.75, 1].
    Eval(s: Capsule3D, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var seg = s.A.Between(s.B);
        var f = AxisFrame(s.A.Lerp(s.B, 0.5), Direction3D(seg.Normalize));
        var theta = uv.U.Turns;
        var h = seg.Magnitude * 0.5;
        var r = s.Radius;
        var v = uv.V;
        var phiB = (0.5 - 0.25 * (v * 4.0)).Turns;
        var phiT = (0.25 - 0.25 * ((v - 0.75) * 4.0)).Turns;
        var local = v <= 0.25
            ? Point3D(phiB.Sin * theta.Cos * r, phiB.Sin * theta.Sin * r, phiB.Cos * r - h)
            : (v >= 0.75
                ? Point3D(phiT.Sin * theta.Cos * r, phiT.Sin * theta.Sin * r, phiT.Cos * r + h)
                : Point3D(theta.Cos * r, theta.Sin * r, (v - 0.5) * 4.0 * h));
        return f.PointInFrame(local);
    }
    ClosedU(s: Capsule3D): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Capsule3D): Boolean => false;

    // CylindricalShell UV: the outer wall up over V in [0, 0.5], then the inner wall back
    // down over [0.5, 1], so one UV rectangle covers both walls and the seam at
    // V = 0.5 is the top rim.
    Eval(s: CylindricalShell, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var f = AxisFrame(s.Center, s.Axis);
        var r = uv.V < 0.5 ? s.OuterRadius : s.InnerRadius;
        var z = (uv.V < 0.5 ? (uv.V * 2.0) - 0.5 : 1.5 - (uv.V * 2.0)) * s.Height;
        var p = PointOnCircle(uv.U.Turns, r);
        return f.PointInFrame(Point3D(p.X, p.Y, z));
    }
    ClosedU(s: CylindricalShell): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: CylindricalShell): Boolean => false;

    //==
    // Polygonal prisms and pyramids
    //
    // These are the payoff of the constant-rate profile walk: because NGonPoint /
    // SquarePoint are linear between vertices, a uniform UV grid puts grid lines
    // exactly on the profile edges and the quad mesh is EXACT, not an approximation.

    Eval(s: RegularPrism, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var p = NGonPoint(uv.U, s.SideCount);
        return s.Frame.PointInFrame(
            Point3D(p.X * s.Radius, p.Y * s.Radius, (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Height));
    }
    ClosedU(s: RegularPrism): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: RegularPrism): Boolean => false;

    // V = 0 is the base ring, V = 1 the apex.
    Eval(s: RegularPyramid, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var p = NGonPoint(uv.U, s.SideCount);
        var r = s.Radius * (1.0 - uv.V);
        return s.Frame.PointInFrame(
            Point3D(p.X * r, p.Y * r, (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Height));
    }
    ClosedU(s: RegularPyramid): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: RegularPyramid): Boolean => false;

    // V = 0 is the square base, V = 1 the apex.
    Eval(s: SquarePyramid, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var p = SquarePoint(uv.U);
        var r = s.BaseLength * 0.5 * (1.0 - uv.V);
        return s.Frame.PointInFrame(
            Point3D(p.X * r, p.Y * r, (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Height));
    }
    ClosedU(s: SquarePyramid): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: SquarePyramid): Boolean => false;

    // The four side walls of a box, as one closed-in-U strip. Size is the FULL
    // extent along each local axis, so the profile is scaled by half of it.
    Eval(s: Box3D, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var p = SquarePoint(uv.U);
        var local = Vector3D(p.X * s.Size.Width * 0.5,
                             p.Y * s.Size.Height * 0.5,
                             (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Size.Depth);
        var w = local.Transform(s.Orientation);
        return (s.Center.X + w.X, s.Center.Y + w.Y, s.Center.Z + w.Z);
    }
    ClosedU(s: Box3D): Boolean => true;
    ClosedV(s: Box3D): Boolean => false;

    //==
    // # The typed polyhedral solids as polygon meshes
    //
    // The Kind dispatch and Frame/Radius placement that turn the value types of
    // `solids.types.plato` into geometry: each named solid looks up its
    // unit-circumradius mesh (the catalog factories of
    // `polyhedra.library.plato` stays the sole vertex source), rescales it to the requested circumscribed radius, and
    // maps it into the solid's frame. The parametric prism / pyramid / antiprism
    // families build their closed meshes directly from their profile parameters —
    // the parametric surface `Eval` above walks the same
    // boundary but is not a closed polyhedral mesh. Triangulation is the standard
    // second hop through `ToTriangleMesh` (`meshes-polygon.library.plato`).
    //
    // Catalog coverage is total: all thirteen Archimedeans and all thirteen
    // Catalans dispatch into a catalog factory (`polyhedra.library.plato`,
    // `polyhedra.library.plato`,
    // `polyhedra.library.plato`). Catalans
    // are rescaled by their measured circumscribed radius and never through
    // `ProjectedToUnitSphere` — they are face-transitive, so projecting would bend
    // their faces out of plane; a uniform scale cannot.

    //==
    // Placement helpers.

    // The mesh with every vertex mapped from frame-local to world coordinates
    // (`PointInFrame`, `transforms.library.plato`); connectivity is untouched.
    TransformedByFrame(self: PolygonMesh3D, f: Frame3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => (self.Positions.Map(p => f.PointInFrame(p)), self.Faces);

    // The largest distance from the origin to a vertex: the circumscribed
    // radius of an origin-centred polyhedron.
    CircumscribedRadius(self: PolygonMesh3D): Number
        => self.Positions.Map(p => p.PositionVector.Magnitude).Reduce(0.0, (acc, m) => acc.Max(m));

    // The mesh rescaled about the origin so its circumscribed radius is one.
    // A uniform scale, NOT ProjectedToUnitSphere: uniform scaling is
    // meaning-preserving for the face-transitive Catalans too, whose vertices
    // genuinely sit at several radii. The empty mesh passes through unchanged.
    ScaledToUnitCircumradius(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => self.VertexCount == 0 ? self : self.ScaledAboutOrigin(1.0 / self.CircumscribedRadius);

    // The empty polygon mesh: the explicit "nothing" mesh (no dispatch arm
    // returns it any more, but callers may still want the zero element).
    // Detect it with `MeshIsEmpty` or `VertexCount == 0`.
    EmptyPolygonMesh(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(Repeat(0, Point3D.Origin),
                              Repeat(0, Repeat(0, VertexIndex(0))));
```
